main_body: Flat stone-brick ground/wall texture tile with staggered courses of rounded stones separated by dark mortar rows; no standing volume.
top_band: none: the column scan shows a repeating stone/mortar pattern (L 143/115/90 stone, L 50-69 mortar) with no object top band, as expected for a seamless terrain texture.
evidence: Kind is terrain, a repeating surface tile and not a standing object, so the top-plus-front contract for standing objects does not apply. Each stone has a light top edge and a darker body, but the tile is a seamless pattern with no receding side faces or fake top surfaces, so nothing violates the contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has 5 distinct colours, a median of 5 per tile and 0% flat-fill coverage. The paving reference has 7 colours, a median of 7 per tile and 80% neutral dark edges, so the candidate is slightly lower on those facts but in the same range. The grass reference (80 colours) is richer, but it is a different material. Each stone is shaded individually with a highlight cap, a mid body and dark mortar in five lightness steps. The dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral (slightly warm greys), which is close to the paving reference's 80%, so the outline reads as a mortar tone rather than a sticker line. A careful artist would accept it next to the paving reference without it looking much thinner.
